title: Three verified application workflows
markdown:
# Three verified application workflows

A development diary about running my existing application workflow end to end with my dot.

This entry follows three application workflows that my dot completed today. All three reached official confirmation pages. They are a focused sample of the day's broader work. Whether they lead to interviews, offers, or income is still unknown.

## What I actually did today

I was working from an existing pipeline: research, fit, tailor, submit, receipt. The source material and application-facts baseline were already in place. For these runs, today's work was to check live openings, prepare two new role-specific resumes, and record what actually completed.

The two new resumes in these reviewed runs were one-page PDFs, tailored for growth and business-development work. Each was rendered and visually checked before upload. The third example continued from materials prepared earlier. That distinction matters in a daily log: these were new application artifacts and completed runs of an existing workflow.

## The workflow I ran

- **Research:** Verify the live role on the official hiring site.
- **Fit:** Compare the requirements with evidence I can support.
- **Tailor:** Select relevant experience and check the final PDF.
- **Submit:** Review the entered form and check for duplicates.
- **Receipt:** Record an official completion signal before counting it.

## Three reviewed submissions

- **Application A, observed 07:41 UTC:** Confirmation page and matching email.
- **Application B, observed 08:53 UTC:** Confirmation page.
- **Application C, observed 09:55 UTC:** Confirmation page and matching email.

Times are rounded observations of the official success pages, not employer-generated timestamps. These three workflows were verified by 09:56 UTC. This entry is not an exhaustive daily count.

## What the live run taught me

### A selected field can still fail validation

One form appeared to have a required role selected, but the first submission returned a definite missing-field error. The selection was corrected in the form, and the second attempt reached the success page. That was one successful application after a rejected attempt. The visible selection alone had not proved the form would accept it.

### Tailoring needs a factual boundary

The new resumes emphasized experience relevant to each opening. They did not turn adjacent experience into claims of sales quotas, closed deals, account ownership, or independent coding mastery. The useful editing work was choosing which verified contributions to explain, and checking that the final document still said exactly that.

### A receipt changes the status

All three reviewed applications had official success pages. Two also had matching acknowledgment emails. For the remaining application, no email had appeared in the immediate check, but the success page already established submission. I kept it in the confirmed total and did not send it again.

### Unknown needs its own state

Other paths remained unresolved: an upload-only path had not reached submission, and a separate retry still had an uncertain outcome. Neither is included among these verified examples. Before repeating a consequential action, I need to establish what the destination actually received.

## What remains open

There is also unfinished infrastructure work around Life Manager. Local capacity remains constrained. Today's application results do not establish that the capacity issue is resolved, and I have not completed a full cloud migration. That work stays open.

## Where I want to focus next

My current priority is frontier AGI companies, with particular attention to business and deployment roles where I can support the fit with real evidence. That is the direction I want to pursue. I am not claiming an affiliation with any of those companies. Today's broader application work is the starting point for a more focused search.

The lesson I am carrying forward is practical: keep the role evidence, the tailored document, the submitted form, and the receipt connected. A useful development diary should let me tell what changed today, what was reused, and what still needs checking.

Written with AI assistance from my dot, using verified records from today's work. Employer names, contact information, and private application details are intentionally omitted.
